report:
## Conclusion

The best available evidence indicates that saw palmetto (Serenoa repens) preparations do **not** provide meaningful, longer-term improvement in benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) symptoms compared with placebo.

The most rigorous evidence comes from the updated Cochrane systematic review (MacDonald et al., 2012), which pooled multiple randomized, placebo-controlled trials, including studies using dose-escalation protocols. It concluded that Serenoa repens performed no better than placebo for improving urinary symptom scores, peak urine flow, or prostate size, even at higher-than-standard doses (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3513282/).

This is corroborated by the large, well-designed CAMUS trial (Complementary and Alternative Medicine for Urological Symptoms), a multicenter, placebo-controlled study that specifically tested escalating doses of saw palmetto extract over an extended 18-month period specifically to assess long-term effects. It found no evidence of a dose-response benefit and no meaningful symptom improvement beyond placebo, though it confirmed the extract's safety even at three times the usual dose (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3716255/).

The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH), a U.S. government evidence-based authority, summarizes this literature similarly: while early small trials suggested modest benefit, larger, higher-quality studies (including CAMUS) and the Cochrane review found saw palmetto no more effective than placebo for BPH-related urinary symptoms (https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/providers/digest/spotlight-on-saw-palmetto-science).

Earlier, smaller meta-analyses (e.g., the 1998 JAMA review) suggested modest short-term benefits, but these studies were generally lower quality, shorter duration, and more heterogeneous, and their positive findings have not been replicated in larger, longer, better-controlled trials.

**Bottom line:** Current high-quality evidence does not support saw palmetto as an effective longer-term treatment for BPH symptoms beyond placebo effect.
